title: The comet and the laser
caption: Comet Lemmon and a laser test at the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A laser beam shoots from ESO's Very Large Telescope into a sky full of stars, with the Milky Way arching overhead. It may look like a futuristic laser cannon aimed at some distant invader, but it was captured during tests of a new laser for the VLT.

The laser was destined to play a key role in the VLT's Laser Guide Star Facility. This system lets astronomers correct most of the disturbance caused by the constantly moving atmosphere, producing much sharper images.

There is a second treat hidden in the picture. Right of center, just below the Small Magellanic Cloud and almost lost among countless stars, sits a small green dot trailing a faint tail to the left. This is Comet Lemmon, then newly discovered and brighter than expected, which was moving slowly through the southern skies.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, which helps a faint comet and the Milky Way show clearly in the same frame as the laser.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The photograph was taken by ESO Photo Ambassador Gerhard Hüdepohl on 14 February 2013, while engineers were testing the laser at Paranal. The same frame also caught Comet Lemmon moving through the southern sky.
alt: A laser beam rises from a large telescope under the Milky Way, with a small green comet with a faint tail right of center below a fuzzy patch of stars.
